title: Experimental identification of the physics that sets the Higgs-mass scale

concept.text: The innovation would be an experimental explanation of why the Higgs field produces the observed electroweak scale. The Standard Model describes this behavior using a Higgs potential, but inserts its mass parameter, μ², without explaining its origin. The target is to discover the particles or interactions responsible and measure how they determine the origin, sign and magnitude of that parameter. Peskin’s 2025 discussion frames this as missing physical understanding of the Higgs boson and electroweak symmetry breaking, rather than a formal inconsistency in the Standard Model.

Supersymmetry and composite-Higgs mechanisms are examples of possible explanations, not mandatory answers. Supersymmetry introduces partner particles whose contributions can cancel quadratic sensitivity to very high energy scales. Composite-Higgs proposals instead connect the Higgs to new underlying dynamics. Either approach would have to be established through measurements linking its new degrees of freedom to the Higgs potential. Discovering an otherwise unexplained particle would not, by itself, identify the physics that sets the Higgs-mass scale.

Proposed scope: this entry requires an experimentally established physical mechanism. An anthropic argument about selection among possible vacua, without an experimentally established mechanism accounting for the Higgs potential, would not meet that scope. This is an evidentiary boundary for the entry, not a claim that such arguments have been scientifically excluded.

significance.text: Identifying the mechanism would turn an unexplained input of the Standard Model into a quantitatively tested account of electroweak symmetry breaking. Its direct significance would be the discovery of new particle content or interactions and an organizing principle connecting them to the Higgs field. A successful explanation could show why this fundamental scale has its observed value, rather than merely extending the list of known particles.

Protection from large corrections and explanation of the observed scale are distinct achievements. The Standard Model supplies no general protection against large corrections from coupled physics at much higher scales. Supersymmetric partner contributions can cancel quadratic ultraviolet sensitivity, but supersymmetry breaking leaves mass-dependent corrections, residual logarithmic sensitivity and potentially substantial tuning. Measuring such cancellation would therefore establish an important protection mechanism without necessarily explaining the value and sign of μ². The stronger discovery sought here must also account for the symmetry-breaking parameters that determine the Higgs potential.

Further consequences would depend on the discovered theory. Under suitable assumptions, including conserved R-parity, a stable lightest supersymmetric particle could be a dark-matter candidate. Establishing that it constitutes cosmological dark matter would still require independent evidence about its interactions and abundance. Precision studies, exploration of additional states and any cosmological applications would be subsequent work; they do not follow automatically from identifying a Higgs-sector mechanism.

The enormous separation between the electroweak and Planck scales is related to this problem, and Peskin explicitly discusses it. However, a statement that gravity is roughly 10^40 times weaker than another force does not specify the same experimental target. The supplied evidence does not establish that numerical comparison, and an explanation of μ² would not automatically constitute a complete theory of gravity.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is to identify the responsible degrees of freedom and reconstruct their quantitative contribution to the Higgs potential. This requires more than observing a new resonance or missing-energy signal: measured masses, couplings and symmetry-breaking relations must connect the new physics to electroweak symmetry breaking. A central scientific barrier is distinguishing a mechanism that stabilizes a scalar mass against high-scale corrections from one that also explains the observed electroweak scale.

Experimental accessibility is another barrier. Weak-scale superpartners can produce LHC signatures, but possible production does not guarantee detection. Realistic spectra can evade bounds derived from simplified models, so a search result must be interpreted with its assumptions about the particle spectrum and decay patterns. Discovering a state would begin the further task of determining whether it belongs to a coherent mechanism for the Higgs potential.

High-scale supersymmetry illustrates a fundamental limit on feasibility. It can remain viable beyond the reach of every collider currently considered feasible, but that survival does not establish a natural explanation of the weak scale. The supplied review explicitly describes high-scale supersymmetry as relinquishing the naturalness argument. Its continued viability must therefore be separated from evidence that it explains μ² without substantial tuning. The sources do not establish that every possible Higgs-scale mechanism is inaccessible, or rule out new experimental methods.

current_state.text: In the review submitted on 16 May 2025 and revised on 10 July 2025, Constantin, Kraml and Mahmoudi report that no supersymmetric particles had been detected. Their account summarizes extensive LHC searches and surviving possibilities; it does not report experimental identification of the mechanism that sets the Higgs-mass scale. Peskin’s paper, submitted on 1 May 2025 and revised on 1 June 2025, likewise describes the particles responsible for electroweak symmetry breaking as unidentified.

The supersymmetry review summarizes ATLAS and CMS simplified-model exclusion bounds reaching approximately 2.4 TeV for gluinos and first-two-generation squarks, 1.3 TeV for stops and sbottoms, and 1 TeV for electroweakinos. These are reported reaches under particular model assumptions, not universal lower mass limits for every supersymmetric spectrum. The review explains that realistic spectra can evade those simplified bounds and that light superpartners remain possible.

The excesses discussed in that review require additional data and are not discoveries. Its conclusion that no currently feasible collider can definitely exclude supersymmetry as a principle of nature concerns the breadth of the framework; it neither predicts an accessible discovery nor demonstrates that supersymmetry explains the weak scale naturally. Both supplied papers are identified in the research as 2025 Nuclear Physics B publications, with arXiv versions available. They provide theoretical discussion and a review of experimental constraints, rather than a demonstrated completion of this innovation.

The supplied evidence establishes a 2025 scientific snapshot. It contains no subsequent search record verifying whether that experimental situation continued through 1 November 2026. Retrieval of the papers on that later date does not update their scientific claims, so the record does not assert a separately verified 2026 discovery or non-discovery.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed convincing demonstration: replicated discovery of new states or a new strong sector, supported through more than one production or decay channel, followed by measurements that quantitatively establish its role in generating the Higgs potential and accounting for the observed electroweak scale. Replication and multiple channels are proposed evidentiary requirements for this record, not acceptance standards established by the supplied papers.
completion_criteria.label: Replicated multichannel discovery explains Higgs potential and electroweak scale

completion_criteria.text: Proposed mechanism test: where cancellation or screening is claimed, measured masses and couplings should test the relevant relations and their contribution to μ². A supersymmetric explanation should identify partner states and test the coupling and symmetry-breaking relations needed for the account. Protection against large corrections alone would constitute a narrower achievement if the observed sign or magnitude of the Higgs mass term still depended on unexplained inputs.
completion_criteria.label: Measured masses and couplings test claimed mechanism relations for μ²

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and interpretation requirements: independent analyses or experiments should recover compatible particle properties and a consistent explanation of the Higgs potential, with uncertainties and model assumptions made explicit. The explanation should state which contributions have been measured, which remain inferred and how remaining parameters affect the result. Finite measurements could establish a mechanism across the tested range; they could not prove its validity at every energy or exclude all alternatives.
completion_criteria.label: Independent analyses recover compatible Higgs-potential explanations with explicit uncertainties

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: an exclusion limit, a simplified-model constraint, an isolated unexplained excess or a dark-matter signal without evidence connecting it to the Higgs potential would not complete this entry. Evidence from another experimental route could qualify if it established that connection. If the responsible physics lies beyond achievable experiments, the proposed demonstration would remain unmet; this is an open feasibility limitation, not grounds for removing the discovery target.
completion_criteria.label: Experimental evidence connects responsible physics to the Higgs potential

related_concepts.text: PHY-04, Laboratory identification of the dark-matter particle, has the most direct possible overlap. A stable lightest superpartner could participate in both discoveries, but its role in the Higgs potential and its identity as cosmological dark matter are separate propositions. The first requires evidence about electroweak symmetry breaking; the second requires additional interaction and abundance evidence. Neither entry should be treated as completed by the other.

Roster-based synthesis: PHY-10, Collider-quality plasma wakefield acceleration, could provide an enabling accelerator capability if it ultimately supported experiments sensitive to the relevant states. Accelerator performance would remain distinct from discovery and quantitative identification of a Higgs-scale mechanism. The supplied material does not establish that this technology would reach the required energies, luminosities or measurement precision.

Roster-based synthesis: PHY-05, A tested microphysical account of the dark-energy scale, also seeks to explain a fundamental scale, but concerns a different physical quantity. PHY-13, A tested mechanism for the cosmic matter excess, concerns the origin of the matter–antimatter imbalance. A future theory might connect either problem to the Higgs sector, but the supplied evidence establishes no such connection; each requires its own quantitative explanation and experimental tests.

Roster-based synthesis: PHY-03, A laboratory proof that gravity is non-classical, and PHY-11, A tested resolution of the black-hole information paradox, address quantum aspects of gravity. The related electroweak-to-Planck hierarchy does not make those targets equivalent to explaining the Higgs mass term. Likewise, observing baryon-number violation in PHY-07 or lepton-number violation in PHY-08 would reveal new physics without, by itself, establishing its responsibility for the Higgs-mass scale.

brief.title: An explanation for a basic scale of particle masses
possible: We could explain why the Higgs field, which gives particles mass, settles at its observed strength. That would mean finding the particles or interactions responsible and measuring how they set the Higgs potential: the field’s energy rules.
why: For particle physicists, this would replace a number inserted into today’s theory by hand with a tested physical explanation. It would reveal an organizing principle connecting new particles or interactions to a fundamental scale in nature.

sources.who: L. Constantin, S. Kraml and F. Mahmoudi
sources.showed: Their review describes searches for supersymmetry, a theory that gives known particles partner particles. Searches exclude many simple scenarios, while more complicated arrangements can evade those limits.
sources.quote:
Despite early hopes that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) would quickly unveil supersymmetric particles, none have been detected
to date.
sources.cited_for: The search limits leave possible partner particles undiscovered.
sources.not_established: No partner particles have been shown to generate the Higgs potential or explain its observed scale.

sources.showed: Peskin argues that the central problem is a missing physical explanation for the Higgs potential. The Standard Model, today’s theory of known particles, leaves its controlling mass parameter unexplained.
sources.cited_for: The target is a physical explanation for the origin, sign and size of the Higgs mass parameter.
sources.not_established: The discussion does not experimentally identify the particles or interactions responsible.

shown: In their 2025 review, Constantin, Kraml and Mahmoudi reported that no supersymmetric partner particles had been detected. Peskin likewise described the physics responsible for the Higgs field’s behavior as unidentified.
missing: Experiments have yet to identify the particles or interactions responsible and measure their contributions to the Higgs potential.
No measured mechanism explains both the sign and size of the parameter that sets the field’s strength.
A discovery has yet to distinguish protection against large changes from an explanation of the observed mass scale.

milestones.label: Repeated discoveries explain the Higgs field’s strength
milestones.explanation: New particles or interactions would have to appear repeatedly through different production or decay routes and quantitatively explain the observed mass scale. This would connect their discovery to the Higgs potential.

milestones.label: Measured properties test the mechanism’s predicted relationships
milestones.explanation: Measured masses and interaction strengths would have to test the predicted relationships, including any claimed cancellations. This would test whether the mechanism explains the mass parameter’s sign and size.

milestones.label: Independent analyses reach compatible explanations
milestones.explanation: Independent analyses or experiments would have to recover compatible particle properties and Higgs potentials, with uncertainties and assumptions explicit. This would establish how securely measurements support the explanation.

milestones.label: Experimental evidence connects the responsible physics to the Higgs potential
milestones.explanation: Experimental evidence would have to establish this connection through whichever route reveals the responsible physics. This would distinguish a physical explanation from a search limit or an unexplained signal.

uncertain: The responsible physics could lie beyond achievable experiments; whether another experimental route could reach it remains open.
There is no agreed threshold for how much delicate cancellation or unexplained parameter dependence an acceptable explanation may retain.

page.title: Experimental determination of the origin of the Higgs mass parameter
page.definition: Experiments would identify the particles or interactions that set the sign and magnitude of μ², the coefficient of |Φ|² in the Higgs potential V(Φ) = μ²|Φ|² + λ|Φ|⁴. This potential gives the energy of the Higgs field Φ. In the Standard Model its minimum occurs at a nonzero field value because μ² is negative and λ is positive. At tree level the measured Higgs boson mass mₕ fixes μ² through μ² = −mₕ²/2.

goal.need: The electroweak scale, of order 100 GeV, affects quantities as different as atomic sizes and radioactive lifetimes. The Standard Model takes this scale from measurements. A more precise Higgs mass sharpens that input. Explaining its origin would show why the Higgs field has the nonzero vacuum value that gives the W and Z bosons their masses and sets a common scale for quark and charged-lepton masses. The individual fermion masses also depend on how strongly each fermion couples to the field.

statements.quote: We do not know why the Higgs boson mass should be as low as it is
statements.context: Section 3.2 identifies unresolved questions motivating the programme to reveal the Higgs boson's properties and underlying physics.

statements.quote: aimed at revealing the deep origin of electroweak (EW) symmetry breaking
statements.context: Volume 1 of the Conceptual Design Report gives this aim for detailed studies of the Higgs boson’s properties.

completion.title: Experimentally identified interactions explain the observed Higgs mass parameter.
completion.criterion: Measured properties of experimentally established new particles or interactions quantitatively account for the origin, negative sign and observed magnitude of μ² in the low-energy Higgs potential, within a specified model and renormalisation prescription. The coefficient must follow from the identified mechanism and measured parameters rather than remain an independent fitted input. Cancellation of large radiative corrections alone does not meet this test.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback; no outside acceptance test for experimentally explaining the origin of μ² was located.
completion.basis: The 2020 European Strategy, 2023 P5 report, supplied 2025 reviews and published collider tests of naturalness were searched for a mechanism-level acceptance test; none was found. This fallback follows Peskin's distinction between explaining μ² and cancelling ultraviolet sensitivity. Published naturalness sum rules test the latter in specified weakly coupled theories.

milestones.title: A Higgs candidate is observed with at least 5σ significance.
milestones.criterion: Observe a signal consistent with production of a Higgs boson at a significance of at least 5σ relative to the background-only hypothesis.
milestones.set_by: Particle-physics discovery convention, documented in the ATLAS glossary and applied in the ATLAS and CMS discovery papers.
milestones.threshold_quote: Five sigma significance is traditionally required to claim a discovery

milestones.title: The Higgs boson's cubic self-coupling is measured with 5% precision.
milestones.criterion: Measure the cubic Higgs self-coupling with relative precision of 5% or better. The coupling may be reported as κλ, its ratio to the Standard Model prediction. P5 gives no confidence-level convention for the 5% target.
milestones.set_by: US High Energy Physics Advisory Panel's 2023 P5 report, section 3.2.4.

milestones.title: A new particle proposed in a Higgs-scale mechanism is observed with at least 5σ significance.
milestones.criterion: Observe a new particle with significance of at least 5σ against the background-only hypothesis. Its measured properties must be consistent with a particle in a specified mechanism for the Higgs mass parameter. Its contribution to μ² remains a separate test.
milestones.set_by: Particle-physics discovery convention, documented in the ATLAS glossary; the convention establishes a particle signal, not its explanation of μ².
milestones.threshold_quote: Five sigma significance is traditionally required to claim a discovery

milestones.title: Measurements determine a new sector's contribution to the Higgs mass parameter.
milestones.criterion: Use measured new-sector parameters to determine the sign and magnitude of that sector’s contribution to μ² in a specified theory and renormalisation prescription. For weakly coupled partner models, test the applicable cancellation relations among partner masses and Higgs couplings. Those relations address the ultraviolet-sensitive terms. The finite contribution must also be determined.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback; searches of the roadmaps and collider naturalness literature found no mechanism-independent acceptance criterion for reconstructing a new sector's contribution to μ².

milestones.title: Nonresonant Higgs boson pair production is observed above 5σ significance.
milestones.criterion: Observe production of two Higgs bosons in a collision, with a significance above 5σ against the hypothesis of zero nonresonant Higgs pair production. The signal is the continuum contribution, which excludes pairs produced by the decay of a new resonance.
milestones.set_by: ATLAS and CMS collaborations, joint High-Luminosity LHC projections for the European Strategy update

not_found: No universally adopted numerical precision or permitted residual tuning for an experimental Higgs-scale explanation was found.
